What Flint does on this phone, and what it can\'t do.

Easy can offer an app break of up to five minutes when no other restriction prevents it. You can confirm ending an Easy session early, or turning off or removing an Easy rule or limit; other protection may still apply.

A Harder break, early end, rule deletion, switch-off or loosening waits 1 minute for the first confirmed change in a block, then 5, then 15 for each later change. For a daily limit, the count lasts until the limit\'s daily reset. After the wait, confirm the change. A granted break lasts up to five minutes and ends sooner if the block ends.
No breaks and no ending early. Turning a rule off, deleting it or loosening it while it runs is saved for after that block ends. It ends when its time is up, or with an available Emergency Pass.
Easy Timers end early with a 2-second hold. Harder Timers wait first, then take the same hold. Hardcore Timers end at expiry, or with an available Emergency Pass.

These rules apply to new commitments. Protection already running when Flint was updated can keep its earlier editing rights until that occurrence ends; older protection without an end time keeps those rights until you choose a finite duration. A Timer marked Legacy can still be ended with a hold.

One Emergency Pass becomes available seven days after you use it. It starts 60 minutes of recovery across all personal protection. After a clock change or restart, eligibility may be later than seven calendar days.

Running sessions and Timers end, and other protection pauses. New schedule occurrences are also suspended during recovery. Counters are kept; the pass is not refunded. Only commitments still naturally active will resume. While the recovery screen is open, choose Resume protection now to end recovery early.
When a Hardcore block is on screen and a pass is available, the block screen shows Review Emergency Pass. Nothing is spent until you confirm.
You can turn off Accessibility, Usage access or display over other apps for Flint in Android Settings. Flint doesn\'t block those settings. Turning them off can stop or weaken blocking.
Flint\'s rules don\'t block your phone app, emergency calling, your Home screen or Settings. If you make calls with another app, make sure it stays unblocked.
Flint\'s rules never block Android\'s uninstall screens, so you can remove Flint at any time.

Flint can\'t stop the date or time being changed. During the same phone boot, Flint times started sessions and scheduled blocks, breaks, Emergency Pass recovery and the wait for the next pass by elapsed time, and clock changes don\'t reset spent opens or pending waits. Saved schedules keep their time zone and stay on Flint\'s saved timeline. Daily time limits use the phone\'s day, so a clock change can move when they reset, and website checks for scheduled rules follow the phone\'s clock. After a phone restart, some access can end, and pass renewal or a daily reset can take longer, because Flint can\'t always tell how much time really passed.
Website rules need Accessibility and a browser whose address bar Flint can read.
Some phones stop background apps to save battery. If blocking stops, the checks on You show what Flint needs.
No account. No analytics. Your lists, rules and history stay on this phone.
